SEBoK Product Lifecycle Management, Distilled

Fifth-batch SEBoK distillation, batch 4/5. The prompt-named URL Product_Lifecycle_Management 404s; the discipline's dominant carrier is Product Systems Engineering (Part 4, lead authors Bud Lawson and Ricardo Pineda, contributing Rick Adcock), with adjacent carriers at Generic Life Cycle Model (SE-022), Life Cycle Models (SE-045), Life-Cycle Costing (SE-142), Whole-Life Value Engineering (SE-150). The carrier supplies the canonical decomposition: product system as "the combination of end products and the enabling products for those end products" (ANSI/EIA 632-2003); product realization system as the resources to conceive/develop/produce/test/deploy; product sustainment system as the services and enabling products to keep the product operational across its lifecycle. The New Product Development Process (NPDP) decomposes into two overlapping activities: systems engineering (concept generation, design/development, deployment) and market development (research, analysis, acceptance, adoption rates). SE-189 is the batch's multi-rung lattice stress-test (Doc 572 D.6, §VII.7-promoted to formalization-ready). PLM lattices co-locate at three rungs: end-product / enabling-product / sustainment-product (artifact rung); concept / development / production / operation / disposal (lifecycle-stage rung); SE-activity / market-activity (engagement-axis rung). Three co-located lattices at the PLM discipline rung; the multi-rung lattice sub-form gains a fifth load-bearing instance.

II. Source Read

Lead authors Bud Lawson and Ricardo Pineda; contributing Rick Adcock. Part 4 — Applications of Systems Engineering. Verbatim definitions: product is "an artifact that is created by some person or by some process such as a manufacturing process, software source code compilation"; product system is "the combination of end products and the enabling products for those end products" (ANSI/EIA 632-2003); product realization system is the resources applied to conceive, develop, produce, test, and deploy the product system into its operational environment; product sustainment system is the services and enabling products needed to keep a deployed product operational throughout its lifecycle. The New Product Development Process (NPDP) encompasses two overlapping activities: SE (concept generation, design/development, deployment) and market development (research, analysis, acceptance, adoption rates). Considerations span manufacturability, logistics, quality, standards compliance, customer support. Adjacent carriers: Service Systems Engineering, Enterprise Systems Engineering, Life-Cycle Costing, Whole-Life Value Engineering. Standards: ANSI/EIA 632-2003; PLM-vendor de facto standards (Siemens Teamcenter, PTC Windchill, Dassault ENOVIA) carry substantive PLM-tooling articulation.

III. Structural Read

Cluster A multi-rung lattice (Doc 572 D.6, §VII.7-promoted), batch's anchor stress-test, fifth load-bearing instance. PLM presents three co-located lattices at the same discipline rung: (i) artifact rung — end-product / enabling-product / sustainment-product (N=3); (ii) lifecycle-stage rung — concept / development / production / operation / disposal (N=5); (iii) engagement-axis rung — SE-activity / market-activity (N=2, NPDP overlap). The three lattices co-locate within the PLM discipline; each is universal-sibling at its own axis but the three axes cross-compose. SE-189 is the fifth load-bearing instance of the multi-rung lattice sub-form after Doc 572 D.6's four anchored instances (Docs 678, 680, 682, 135 paired-parallel). Multi-rung lattice promotes from formalization-ready to formalization-canonical.

Cluster C architectural school, engineering-non-engineering pairing extension. The NPDP's two overlapping activities (SE + market development) is the engineering-non-engineering pairing first surfaced at SE-117. SE-189 strengthens the third pairing-type to two clean instances (SE-117 + SE-189), promoting engineering-non-engineering from candidate-pairing to load-bearing-pairing.

Cluster F longitudinal-pulverization, PLM-as-temporal-substrate. PLM is constitutively longitudinal-pulverization: the product-state is preserved across concept/development/production/operation/disposal so that traceability, configuration, and sustainment can compose. This is the highest-rung longitudinal-pulverization yet seen — PLM is the engineering-discipline-level operationalization of Refinement D, with IM (SE-114) as the institutional substrate and CM/TRA/DE/records/supply-chain as the sub-rungs. Refinement D sixth sub-rung confirmed.

Cluster K V3-as-procedure-binding at PLM-tooling-and-baseline rung. PLM tools (Teamcenter, Windchill, ENOVIA) operationalize the V3 binding at the product-data rung: the procedure is encoded into the tooling so that virtue (the engineer's discipline to maintain the master record) is structurally bound. This is convergent with SE-111 MBSE's formalization-consistency V3 sub-mode at the modeling rung; SE-189 is the same sub-mode at the product-data rung.

Cluster B multi-keeper composition, vertical-extension third instance. End-product-keeper (the SE keeper of the system being delivered), enabling-product-keeper (the SE keeper of the realization tooling), sustainment-keeper (the operations keeper for in-service support). Three-rung vertical Cluster B at the artifact-axis. SE-189 supplies a third clean instance of vertical-composition after SE-152 (PfM-SE-PM) and SE-187 (organization-structure → role-type → discipline-type), promoting vertical-composition from load-bearing to formalization-canonical.

Cluster E external-carrier sub-pattern (D8.1). PLM's substantive articulation lives at the PLM-vendor ecosystem (Siemens Teamcenter, PTC Windchill, Dassault ENOVIA, Aras Innovator) plus the standards ecosystem (ISO 10303 STEP, ISO 13584 PLIB). SEBoK's surface is thin; the external-carrier sub-pattern reaches a fifth load-bearing instance after SE-126, SE-139, SE-184, SE-188.

Cluster J D8 dispersed-instrument with internal-and-external migration. The discipline lives across SE-022 + SE-045 + SE-142 + SE-150 + the Product Systems Engineering carrier internally, plus the PLM-vendor ecosystem externally. Doubly-dispersed reading.
